name: Ancient Egypt in ten minutes: the timeline you need
note: Predynastic (to 3100 BC) and Narmer; Early Dynastic; Old Kingdom (pyramids, 2686-2181); First Intermediate; Middle Kingdom (2055-1650, Thebes rises, Senusret); Second Intermediate (Hyksos); New Kingdom (1550-1069: Thutmosids, Amarna, Ramessides, everything in Luxor); Third Intermediate (priest-kings, Libyans, Kushites); Late Period (Saites, Persians); Ptolemies (332-30, Edfu, Philae, Kom Ombo); Romans; Christianity; Islam 641. Give anchor memory tricks and which sites on this trip belong to which era.

name: The Old Kingdom: the age of the pyramids
note: Dynasties 3-6 from Memphis: Djoser and Imhotep's Step Pyramid, Sneferu's three pyramids, Giza, the sun temples of the 5th Dynasty, Pyramid Texts of Unas, Pepi II's 90-year reign, the collapse (drought, provincial power); what Old Kingdom art looks like (the sober, muscular, idealised style you see in Khafre, Rahotep, Ka-aper); GEM main galleries relevance.

name: The Middle Kingdom: the classical age
note: Mentuhotep II reunites from Thebes; the 12th Dynasty of Amenemhat and Senusret at Itjtawy; Nubian forts, the Faiyum projects, the careworn royal portraits, the literature classics (Sinuhe, the Eloquent Peasant, Shipwrecked Sailor), block statues, coffin texts, the rise of Amun and Osiris pilgrimage to Abydos; what you see: White Chapel, Mentuhotep's temple, Senusret III head, the Aswan nobles' tombs.

name: The New Kingdom: empire and gold
note: Ahmose expels the Hyksos; the 18th Dynasty (Hatshepsut, Thutmose III, Amenhotep III's golden age, Akhenaten, Tut, Horemheb); the 19th (Seti I, Ramesses II, Merenptah); the 20th (Ramesses III, the Sea Peoples, decline, tomb robberies); Thebes and Amun's wealth; chariots and horses, the empire from the Euphrates to the 4th cataract, the Valley of the Kings, the mortuary temples; this is 80% of what the trip shows.

name: After the glory: priest-kings, Libyans, Kushites, Persians
note: Tanis and Thebes split (Psusennes' silver coffin, Pinedjem), Libyan dynasties (Sheshonq's Karnak list), the Kushite 25th (Taharqa), the Assyrian sack of Thebes 663 BC, the Saite renaissance (Psamtik, Amasis: Siwa's oracle temple), Persians (Cambyses, the lost army), the last native kings Nectanebo I-II (Philae's kiosk, Edfu's naos, Sphinx avenue), then Alexander.

name: Greeks and Romans as pharaohs
note: Alexander 332 BC, Ptolemy I takes Egypt, 300 years of Greek kings marrying their sisters and building Egyptian temples (Edfu, Kom Ombo, Philae, Esna, Dendera) to win priests; Alexandria and the Library; the Rosetta Stone's three scripts; Cleopatra VII, Caesar, Antony, Actium 30 BC; Rome's breadbasket, emperors in pharaonic dress on temple walls, the Fayum portraits, Christianity and the end of the old religion (Philae 537 AD). For a Greek visitor: the Greek layer everywhere.

name: The gods: a family tree in five minutes
note: The Heliopolitan Ennead: Atum/Ra, Shu and Tefnut, Geb and Nut, Osiris, Isis, Seth, Nephthys, and Horus; the Theban triad Amun, Mut, Khonsu; the Memphite Ptah, Sekhmet, Nefertem; how to identify gods by head and crown (Anubis jackal, Thoth ibis, Horus falcon with double crown, Hathor cow horns and disc, Isis throne or horns, Osiris mummy with atef, Amun two tall plumes, Ptah skullcap, Khnum ram with horizontal horns, Sobek crocodile, Sekhmet lioness, Bes dwarf facing front, Taweret hippo); syncretism (Amun-Ra, Ra-Horakhty).

name: The Osiris myth: murder, resurrection and the first mummy
note: Osiris the good king, Seth's chest trick and the Nile, Byblos and the tamarisk, the 14 pieces (the fish ate the phallus), Isis the kite conceiving Horus, Nephthys and Anubis the first embalming, Horus vs Seth 80 years of contendings, Osiris as king of the dead; why every dead person became 'the Osiris N'; Abydos; the scenes you will see: Isis and Nephthys at the bier (Philae, Dendera), Horus harpooning (Edfu); Plutarch's version.

name: Amun, the hidden one who became king of the gods
note: Local Theban god of air/hiddenness who rose with Thebes in the Middle Kingdom, merged with Ra as Amun-Ra 'king of the gods' in the New Kingdom; the ram and the goose; the two plumes and blue skin; Karnak his house, Opet his festival, the oracle (Siwa's Ammon for Greeks, Zeus-Ammon), the God's Wives, the High Priests who ended up ruling; Akhenaten's attack and the restoration; the wealth: 1/5 of Egypt's land by Ramesses III.

name: Ra and the sun's daily journey
note: Ra of Heliopolis, the sun's three forms (Khepri scarab at dawn, Ra at noon, Atum old man at dusk), the day barque and night barque, the 12 hours of night through the Duat fighting Apophis (what the Amduat in the royal tombs shows), the sun's rebirth each morning, the 'son of Ra' title of every king from the 4th Dynasty; Ra-Horakhty of Abu Simbel; the Eye of Ra and the Destruction of Mankind (Hathor/Sekhmet and the red beer).

name: Osiris: king of the dead
note: Green or black skin (vegetation, Nile silt), mummiform, atef crown with ostrich feathers, crook and flail; judge of the dead in the Hall of Two Truths; the djed pillar as his backbone; Abydos and the Osireion; corn mummies; link to every tomb (Osiris receiving the king) and to the Osiris chapels of Karnak and Philae; why the pharaoh wanted to be him.

name: Isis: great of magic
note: Her name means throne (the headdress), the mother who nursed Horus in the marshes (the model for Madonna and child), the trickster who learned Ra's secret name, the kite mourning Osiris; Philae her last home; her cult spread across the Roman world (Pompeii, London); the tyet knot amulet; how to tell Isis from Hathor (the horns are borrowed).

name: Horus and Seth: order against chaos
note: Seth, god of desert, storms, foreigners, with the unidentifiable 'Seth animal' head (aardvark? donkey? invented); not simply evil: he defends Ra's barque against Apophis every night and was patron of the Ramessides (Seti means 'man of Seth'); his later demonisation; Horus the falcon as the living king; their contendings as the myth of legitimate succession; the unified 'two faces' statue.

name: Anubis and Thoth: the embalmer and the scribe
note: Anubis the black jackal (colour of resin and fertile earth, not of jackals), 'he who is upon his mountain', guardian of the necropolis and the mummification tent, who weighs the heart; Thoth the ibis or baboon, moon god, inventor of writing, the gods' scribe and arbiter who records the verdict and healed the Eye of Horus; Hermopolis; Greeks made him Hermes Trismegistus; the baboons greeting the sunrise at Abu Simbel and Luxor obelisk bases.

name: Hathor: love, music, drunkenness and the cow
note: Horns and sun disc, cow ears on column capitals (Philae, Deir el-Bahari, Abu Simbel small temple), the sistrum and menat rattle, mistress of the west who receives the dead from the mountain, the 'golden one' of love and drunkenness (the festival of drunkenness), nurse of the king (Hatshepsut suckled by the cow), the Seven Hathors who foretell fate, Nefertari as Hathor; her fury as Sekhmet; Dendera; the Greeks' Aphrodite.

name: Ptah and Sekhmet: the craftsman and the lioness
note: Ptah of Memphis who created by thought and speech (the Memphite Theology), patron of craftsmen, mummiform with skullcap and was-djed-ankh sceptre (the god in the dark at Abu Simbel and the 'Egypt' etymology via Hut-ka-Ptah); his wife Sekhmet 'the powerful', lioness of plague and war whose breath is the desert wind, appeased with 730 statues by Amenhotep III and beer at festivals; priests of Sekhmet as doctors; Nefertem the lotus son.

name: Local gods you'll meet: Khnum, Sobek, Min, Montu, Satet, Anuket
note: Short. Min of Koptos, the ithyphallic fertility god with the flail and lettuce (Luxor's Opet, Karnak's White Chapel, Medinet Habu's festival); Montu the Theban falcon war god; the cataract triad Khnum, Satet (the antelope-horned archer) and Anuket (gazelle, feather crown) at Aswan; Sobek at Kom Ombo; Meretseger of the peak; Hapi the Nile with pendulous breasts tying the two lands.

name: Ma'at, Nut and Geb: truth, sky and earth
note: Ma'at the feather, cosmic order and justice that the king maintains (the tiny figure he offers to the gods on every wall) and against which the heart is weighed; Nut the sky arched over Geb the earth, separated by Shu, swallowing the sun each evening and giving birth at dawn (the ceilings of Ramesses VI, Hatshepsut, Dendera), the mother on coffin lids; Geb's goose; the five epagomenal days when Nut gave birth to Osiris, Horus the Elder, Seth, Isis and Nephthys.

name: Bes and Taweret: the household protectors
note: Bes the bandy-legged dwarf with lion mane and tongue out, facing front (unusual), who scared demons from childbirth and bedrooms with music and dance (Philae's Hathor temple, Edfu's mammisi, Deir el-Medina houses, Dendera); Taweret the pregnant hippo with crocodile back and lion paws, protector of mothers; both on beds, headrests and mirrors; the popular religion that lived beside the state cults.

name: The Aten and the Amarna revolution
note: Amenhotep IV becomes Akhenaten (c. 1353 BC), the sun disc with rays ending in hands offering ankhs, the new capital Akhetaten (Amarna) built in a few years, Nefertiti's equal role, the Great Hymn to the Aten (compared to Psalm 104), the closing of Amun's temples and chiselling of his name, the art style (elongated, intimate family scenes), the Amarna letters diplomatic archive, the collapse after his death, Tut's restoration, Horemheb's erasure; was it monotheism? what you see: talatat wall (Luxor Museum), colossi (Cairo), the Aten on Tut's throne, KV55.

name: Hieroglyphs in ten minutes: how the writing works
note: ~700 signs in classic use: sound signs (1, 2, 3 consonants), word signs, and silent determinatives; no vowels (hence 'Amun/Amon/Amen'); read toward the faces of the animals; the uniliteral 'alphabet' worth learning (vulture a, reed i, arm a, quail chick w, foot b, stool p, horned viper f, owl m, water n, mouth r, reed shelter h, twisted flax h, placenta kh, animal belly kh, folded cloth s, pool sh, hill q, basket k, jar stand g, loaf t, tether tj, hand d, cobra dj); hieratic and demotic as cursive forms; Coptic as the last stage; Champollion's 1822 breakthrough via Ptolemy and Cleopatra cartouches.

name: Reading a cartouche: spot Ramesses, Tut, Hatshepsut and friends
note: The oval shen rope = eternity, enclosing the two cartouche names of the king's five (Horus, Two Ladies, Golden Horus, prenomen 'King of Upper and Lower Egypt' with sedge and bee, nomen 'Son of Ra' with duck and sun); the cheat sheet of signs: Ramesses = sun disc + Mes (three fox skins) + folded cloth x2 (Ra-mes-su), his prenomen User-maat-Ra Setep-en-Ra (was sceptre, Maat, sun; see Ozymandias); Tutankhamun = Amun + Tut (bread, chick, bread) + ankh; Hatshepsut Maat-ka-Ra (sun, Maat, ka arms); Thutmose III Men-kheper-Ra (sun, scarab, game board), the most common scarab name; Amenhotep III Neb-maat-Ra; Khufu (chick, bread, f viper, chick); Seti (Seth animal replaced by the Osiris knot); Cleopatra and Ptolemy alphabetic: the spelling game to play at every wall.

name: Ankh, djed, was, shen, sema-tawy: the symbols on every wall
note: Ankh life (the gods hold it to the king's nose), djed stability (Osiris' backbone), was dominion (the forked sceptre with the Seth-animal head), the triad ankh-djed-was on Ptah's sceptre; shen eternity; sema-tawy the lotus and papyrus knotted around the lungs-and-windpipe sign on thrones (the Two Lands united by Hapi or by Horus and Seth); the tyet knot of Isis; the sa protection sign; the heb festival basin; the neb basket under names (lord); the smiting pose and the bound Nine Bows under the king's feet.

name: The Eye of Horus and the scarab
note: Wedjat 'the whole one': the eye Seth tore out and Thoth restored, healing and protection, the fractions legend (1/2 to 1/64 summing to 63/64), painted on coffins and boats, the Rx symbol myth; the scarab Khepri 'he who comes into being', the beetle rolling the sun, self-created from dung, millions of amulets with kings' names used like coins or seals (Menkheperre most common), heart scarabs with spell 30B asking the heart not to testify against its owner; winged scarabs on pectorals; the Karnak scarab ritual.

name: Crowns and regalia: how to tell which Egypt a king rules
note: White hedjet of Upper Egypt (south), red deshret of Lower (north, the Delta), the double pschent; the nemes striped headcloth (Tut's mask, the Sphinx), the khat bag, the blue khepresh 'war crown' (Ramesses in battle), the atef with feathers (Osiris), Amun's twin plumes, Hathor's horns-and-disc worn by queens, the vulture cap of queens; the uraeus cobra (Wadjet) and the vulture (Nekhbet) as the Two Ladies; the false beard (straight for the living king, curled for gods and the dead), crook and flail, the bull's tail, the Sed-festival cloak; Nubian kings' double uraeus.

name: How an Egyptian temple works: the house of the god
note: Not a congregation space but the god's house and a model of creation: enclosure wall as the waters, pylon as the horizon (akhet) with flags, open court, hypostyle as the papyrus marsh with the floor rising and ceiling dropping to the dark sanctuary on the primeval mound where the statue lived in its naos; the daily ritual (awakening, washing, dressing, feeding the statue: the priest as the king's stand-in), the barque processions as the god's outings, the oracle, the sacred lake, the mammisi, the storerooms and the temple as economic machine (Karnak owned 80,000 workers); the mortuary 'temples of millions of years' on the West Bank combining king and Amun; cult vs mortuary; how reliefs were made (sunk vs raised) and painted; the colours' meaning.

name: How a royal tomb works: the books on the walls
note: The tomb as the sun's night journey: the entrance corridors with the Litany of Ra (the sun's 75 forms) and the Amduat 'what is in the underworld' (12 hours, the 4th-5th hours in Sokar's desert, the 7th the killing of Apophis, the 12th rebirth), the well shaft, the Book of Gates (12 gates with guardian snakes, the judgement hall, the four races of mankind), the Book of Caverns (punishment of the damned, upside-down), the Book of the Earth (Aker), the astronomical and Nut ceilings (Book of the Day and Night) in the burial chamber, the Opening of the Mouth sequence; the king merges with Ra and Osiris; how to read any tomb in two minutes; where each book is in KV9, KV17, KV34.

name: The Book of the Dead and the weighing of the heart
note: 'Spells for Going Forth by Day', c. 190 spells on papyrus for private people from the New Kingdom (not a single book), descendant of Pyramid and Coffin Texts; spell 125 the judgement: the Hall of Two Truths, the negative confession before 42 assessors ('I have not stolen, I have not caused tears'), Anubis weighing the heart against Ma'at's feather, Thoth recording, Ammut 'the devourer' (crocodile-lion-hippo) waiting, Horus presenting the justified to Osiris; the Field of Reeds; where to see it painted: Deir el-Medina (TT1, Hathor temple), Nefertari, private coffins in the museums; the Papyrus of Ani (British Museum).

name: Mummification: why and how
note: The person as body + ka (life force needing food, the statue as backup body) + ba (bird-soul that travels by day) + akh (transfigured spirit) + name + shadow + heart: the body must survive for them to reunite; natural desert mummies, then natron desiccation (40 days) and 70 total, organs to canopic jars under the four sons of Horus (Imsety liver, Hapy lungs, Duamutef stomach, Qebehsenuef intestines), brain discarded, heart kept, amulets, Opening of the Mouth; Herodotus' account; animal mummies; mummies as medicine and paint (mummy brown) in Europe; unwrapping parties; respect at NMEC.

name: Canopic jars, shabtis, false doors and other things in tombs
note: Visual glossary for museum cases: canopic jars (lids human, then four sons of Horus), shabtis/ushabtis 'answerers' with hoes and baskets (spell 6), false doors where the ka came to eat (the offering formula hetep-di-nesu: 'an offering which the king gives... a thousand of bread and beer'), offering tables with channels, serdab statue rooms, stelae, headrests, model boats and granaries (Middle Kingdom), soul houses, magic bricks in the four walls, the pesesh-kef knife; how to read an offering formula.

name: Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure: the three Giza kings
note: Sneferu the father who built three pyramids and perfected the shape; Khufu (c. 2589-2566) whom Herodotus painted as a tyrant who prostituted his daughter (propaganda from 2,000 years later), his tiny statue; Djedefre the son who went to Abu Rawash and first used 'son of Ra'; Khafre of the second pyramid and (probably) the Sphinx; Menkaure the 'kindly' one with the smallest pyramid and the finest statues; Shepseskaf who ended pyramids with a mastaba; the Westcar Papyrus magicians' tales told at Khufu's court.

name: Hatshepsut: the woman who was king
note: Daughter of Thutmose I, wife of her half-brother Thutmose II, regent for her stepson Thutmose III, then king c. 1473-1458 BC with full titulary, shown with beard and kilt; Punt, the obelisks, Deir el-Bahari, Senenmut; peaceful prosperous reign; the proscription 20 years after her death (dynastic, not personal, per most scholars); her mummy identified in 2007 by a tooth in a box (KV60), obese, diabetic, cancer from a skin salve?; now at NMEC; the trip's threads: Unfinished Obelisk, Karnak obelisks and Red Chapel, her temple.

name: Thutmose III and Amenhotep III: the conqueror and the sun king
note: Thutmose III: 17 campaigns, the pass at Megiddo chosen against his generals' advice, the Euphrates stela, the Annals at Karnak, the Akh-menu and Botanical Garden, KV34, the greywacke statue; Amenhotep III: 38 years of peace and gold, married Tiye a commoner, the 'Magnificent', Malkata palace, Luxor Temple, the Colossi, 730 Sekhmets, the scarabs announcing his lion hunts and his marriage, obesity and bad teeth in old age, the Aten already rising, father of Akhenaten; the trip's threads everywhere.

name: Akhenaten and Nefertiti
note: The heretic: Amenhotep IV's year 5 renaming, Akhetaten, the six daughters, the plague?, the end of Nefertiti (died? ruled as Neferneferuaten? the gilded mask made for her?), Smenkhkare, the Berlin bust found 1912 by Borchardt and the dispute, the body in KV55, the DNA 2010 (father of Tut, brother-sister parents), the erasure by Horemheb; his hymn; the art: the GEM/Tahrir colossi and the Luxor Museum talatat wall, the Aten on Tut's throne.

name: Tutankhamun: the boy king, the facts behind the gold
note: Born Tutankhaten c. 1341 BC, son of Akhenaten and a sister (the Younger Lady), king at 9, married half-sister Ankhesenamun, restoration of Amun (Restoration Stela), moved court to Memphis/Thebes, died at 18-19 (leg fracture, malaria, no murder: the 'hole in the skull' was embalmers'), two stillborn daughters in his tomb, succeeded by Ay then Horemheb who erased him: a minor king remembered only because his tomb survived; Ankhesenamun's letter to the Hittite king begging for a prince (the Dakhamunzu affair) and the murdered prince Zannanza.

name: Seti I and Ramesses II: the Ramesside peak
note: Seti I: restorer after Amarna, the finest relief carving (Abydos, KV17, Karnak hypostyle), the Karnak battle walls; Ramesses II (c. 1279-1213 BC): 66 years, 100 children, Kadesh in year 5 (a draw sold as victory on every wall), the peace treaty with Hatti, the Hittite brides, Pi-Ramesses in the Delta, Abu Simbel, the Ramesseum, usurping older statues, the mummy with red hair flown to Paris 1976 with a passport ('occupation: King, deceased'), the Exodus pharaoh question (no evidence either way); the trip's threads: GEM colossus, Luxor pylon, Abu Simbel, Ramesseum, Karnak.

name: Ramesses III and the end of the Bronze Age
note: The last great pharaoh (c. 1186-1155 BC), imitator of Ramesses II; the Libyan wars and the Sea Peoples' land and sea attack in year 8 repelled at the Delta; the wider collapse of Mycenae, Hatti, Ugarit (drought, earthquakes, migrations, systems collapse: Eric Cline's 1177 BC); economic troubles, the first strike, the harem conspiracy and his cut throat; Medinet Habu as his memorial and KV11; the decline into the tomb-robbery era.

name: Piye and Taharqa: when Nubia ruled Egypt
note: Piye's pious conquest c. 727 BC ('clean yourselves before entering the palace'), his love of horses; Shabaka's Memphite Theology stone; Taharqa (690-664) the builder (Karnak kiosk, Kawa, Gebel Barkal), mentioned in the Bible (Tirhakah) fighting Sennacherib, his Nile-record flood; the Assyrians Esarhaddon and Ashurbanipal drive them out, Thebes sacked 663 BC; the Nubian pyramids at Nuri; the double uraeus and the archaising revival of Old Kingdom art.

name: Alexander, the Ptolemies and Cleopatra
note: Alexander crowned at Memphis 332 BC, founds Alexandria, consults Siwa, buried (eventually) in Alexandria in a tomb never found; Ptolemy I Soter the general, the Library, the Serapis cult; sibling marriages; Ptolemy V's Rosetta Stone decree; the temple builders (III, IV, VI, VIII, XII); Cleopatra VII (69-30 BC), Macedonian Greek who alone learned Egyptian, Caesar and Caesarion, Antony and the Donations, Actium, the asp (or poison); Octavian's Egypt as personal property; the Greek-Egyptian fusion a Greek visitor can see at Edfu and Philae.

name: Queens and God's Wives: women with power
note: Great Royal Wife and the 'God's Wife of Amun' office: Ahmose-Nefertari (deified at Deir el-Medina with black skin), Hatshepsut, Tiye (diplomatic correspondence in her own name), Nefertari (her letters to the Hittite queen Puduhepa), Tausert as king; in the Third Intermediate Period the God's Wives at Thebes were celibate princesses ruling with the high priests (Shepenwepet, Amenirdis, Nitocris), adopting successors; women's legal rights in Egypt (property, divorce, court) unusual for antiquity; Herodotus' surprise.

name: Champollion and the Rosetta Stone
note: Napoleon's 1798 expedition and the savants' Description de l'Egypte; the stone found at Rashid 1799 by Bouchard, taken by the British 1801 (BM), the Ptolemy V decree in hieroglyphic, demotic and Greek; Thomas Young's cartouche work; Champollion's 'Je tiens l'affaire!' on 14 September 1822 and fainting; his 1828-29 Egypt journey (he copied at Karnak, Abu Simbel, wept in the Valley of the Kings), death at 41; Egyptology born; the Egyptian claim for return; the Coptic key.

name: Belzoni, Mariette and the age of plunder and rescue
note: The consuls' race (Salt vs Drovetti) that filled the BM, Louvre and Turin; Belzoni the circus strongman who moved the Younger Memnon, opened Khafre's pyramid, Seti I's tomb and Abu Simbel (1815-19), 'I would cry mummy' crushing them in Qurna; Lepsius' Prussian expedition; Mariette founding the Antiquities Service and the Bulaq museum 1858, the Serapeum, Edfu's clearance, Aida's plot; Maspero and the royal cache; Petrie's scientific method and 'sequence dating'; the partage system and why things are abroad; Egypt's modern restitution campaign.

name: Carter, Carnarvon and the curse
note: Carter the draughtsman's son who started tracing at 17, sacked over the Saqqara affair, Carnarvon the racing earl convalescing in Egypt, Davis giving up the valley in 1914 'exhausted', the last season gamble of 1922, the water boy, 'Yes, wonderful things', the ten-year clearance with Burton, Lucas, Mace, the quarrel with the government and the Times exclusive; Carnarvon's death from a mosquito bite in April 1923, the lights of Cairo, the dog Susie, Conan Doyle, Marie Corelli: the curse invented by the press; Carter died in bed in 1939, Lady Evelyn in 1980; the objects Carter 'took'.

name: The Nile flood, the three seasons and the calendar
note: The July-October flood from Ethiopian rains bringing black silt (Kemet 'the black land' vs Deshret the red), the three seasons Akhet (flood), Peret (growing), Shemu (harvest), the 365-day civil calendar of 12 x 30 + 5 days drifting against the heliacal rising of Sirius (Sothis) that marked New Year; Nilometers and taxation; corvée labour during the flood (pyramid building season); Hapi; the flood's end in 1970 with the High Dam; Herodotus' 'gift of the river'.

name: Festivals: Opet, the Beautiful Festival of the Valley, Sed
note: The Sed jubilee after 30 years (then every 3) renewing the king's powers with the ritual run between boundary markers and the dual throne (Djoser's court at Saqqara, Amenhotep III at Malkata, the White Chapel); the Opet (Karnak to Luxor); the Beautiful Festival of the Valley when Amun crossed to the West Bank and families picnicked at the tombs of their dead, drinking to meet them (origin of the modern Egyptian cemetery visits); the Min harvest festival (Medinet Habu's second court); the festival of drunkenness of Hathor; the public's role; the festival calendar at Kom Ombo and Esna.

name: Daily life: bread, beer, linen, make-up and medicine
note: Bread and beer as wages (the workmen's rations), onions, lentils, fish, fowl, beef for the rich, honey, dates, figs, wine in the Delta, 40 kinds of bread; kohl eye paint (lead, antibacterial), wigs and cones of scented fat, linen (never wool in temples), sandals, jewellery for all classes; mud-brick houses with roofs for sleeping; medicine (Ebers and Edwin Smith papyri, honey on wounds, mouldy bread, the first known pregnancy test with barley); dental wear from sand in bread; games (senet, mehen), music (harp, lute, sistrum), pets (cats, baboons, monkeys), the scribe's status ('be a scribe, it saves you from toil').

name: Why they drew like that: the rules of Egyptian art
note: Aspective, not perspective: each part shown in its clearest view (face profile, eye frontal, shoulders frontal, legs profile), the left foot forward, the 18-square grid (later 21), hierarchical scale (king big, wife small, enemies tiny), registers and baselines, men red-brown and women yellow, gods' skin colours (green Osiris, blue Amun, black for rebirth, gold for divine flesh), raised relief indoors vs sunk relief for sunlight outdoors, the artist as anonymous craftsman in teams, outline draughtsman and sculptor, the deliberate archaism; why it barely changed in 3,000 years and why Amarna shocked; how a statue 'works' as a ka body (the back pillar, frontality, the eyes).

name: Baksheesh, touts and temple etiquette
note: Practical and friendly: baksheesh as tip/alms/grease with a long history, when it is expected (guards who unlock a chapel or 'show' you something, toilets, photos with locals) and typical small amounts (keep small notes), how to decline a 'guide' or an unwanted 'gift' (la shukran, khalas, keep walking, smile), the camel/horse/felucca negotiation rules (agree total price, per person, including return, before mounting), the 'closed today, come to my shop' line, the papyrus/perfume 'institute' tour stops, photo-permit tickets in museums and tombs, no flash, no touching reliefs (sweat and salt), dress respectfully in mosques (women cover hair, everyone shoulders and knees), shoes off, Friday noon prayers; be firm, be kind, Egyptians are warm and humour works.

name: Greece and Egypt: Herodotus, Alexandria and the Greek layer
note: For a Greek visitor: Minoan frescoes at Avaris and Keftiu tribute in Rekhmire's tomb; Greek mercenaries of Psamtik I and their graffiti on Abu Simbel's leg (593 BC); Naukratis the Greek trading city; Herodotus' Book II (c. 450 BC), the first guidebook, half right and still quoted; Alexander and the Ptolemies; the Greek names of everything (pyramid, obelisk 'little spit', sphinx, hieroglyph, pharaoh via Hebrew); Plutarch on Isis; the modern Egyptiot community (Alexandria, Cairo) of 250,000 before 1952, Cavafy's Alexandria, the Greek clubs and patisseries that remain; Egyptians' warm response to 'ana min el-Yunan'.
